data.narrative:
Looking Glass, a Series A chip design company founded by Shawn Frayne, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies in the same sector and stage, with particular focus on SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B).

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $30M raised proxy, implying $60M. Peer-median analysis, using three same-sector, same-stage companies, yields a median valuation of $2.3B with a range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (20.5x median) is not applicable here, as Looking Glass does not publicly disclose revenue figures typical of private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $51M (floor) to $2.7B (ceiling), with a median of $1.2B. This wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty in the private chip design market, where valuations remain highly stage- and traction-dependent. The peer-median method carries more weight given the direct comparability of SambaNova, Rebellions, and d-Matrix; however, the stage-progression floor remains relevant as a sanity check against round structure. Key uncertainties include differentiation of Looking Glass's technology versus the peer set, capital efficiency trajectory, and whether the company has achieved product-market validation milestones beyond capital raised.
